decisions.reason: As a relatively low-investment dietary supplement with weaker visible commitment than the firm's drug products, it is the easiest for management to discontinue despite some sunk branding costs.
Its explicit pharmacy-focused launch and dedicated web presence create enough public commitment that management is likely to continue it unless results are clearly poor.
Because it was introduced as a new joint-health offer and then given its own page, management has moderate reputational and brand investment pushing it to persist.
Management has publicly framed it as an innovative and new addition to the Trivital line, which raises commitment and supports blaming any weakness on temporary market factors.

As a generic cardiovascular medicine in the firm's core pharmaceutical business, with high regulatory and commercial investment and problems that can be attributed to a temporary external issue, it is unlikely to be withdrawn.
An over-the-counter migraine triptan fits closely with the firm's core pharmaceutical capabilities and likely involved meaningful approval and launch costs, encouraging continued support.
